cases.sentence: ___ осветил лицо Анны в то время, как она почувствовала на себе его взгляд.
cases.translation: A peculiar radiance lit up Anna's face just as she felt his gaze upon her.
cases.explain: Блеск is the subject performing осветил (lit up), hence nominative.

cases.sentence: «Не правда ли, необыкновенно хорош», — сказал Степан Аркадьевич, заметив, что Левин взглядывал на портрет. «Я не видал лучше ___».
cases.translation: 'Isn't it extraordinarily good,' said Stepan Arkadyich, noticing that Levin kept glancing at the portrait. 'I have never seen a better portrait.'
cases.explain: The comparative лучше (better than) governs the genitive case, hence портрета.

cases.sentence: Я вас давно знаю и люблю, и по ___ со Стивой, и за вашу жену.
cases.translation: I have known and loved you for a long time, both out of friendship with Stiva, and for your wife's sake.
cases.explain: The preposition по (out of/through) governs the dative case, hence дружбе.

cases.sentence: Я знала ее очень мало времени, но она оставила во мне ___ прелестного цветка, именно цветка, и она уж скоро будет матерью.
cases.translation: I knew her only a very short time, but she left in me the impression of a lovely flower, precisely a flower, and she will soon be a mother.
cases.explain: Впечатление is the direct object of оставила (left), hence accusative (identical in form to the nominative for this neuter noun).

cases.sentence: У меня не настолько широкое сердце, чтобы полюбить целый приют с гаденькими ___.
cases.translation: My heart isn't broad enough to love a whole orphanage full of unpleasant little girls.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case, hence девочками (plural instrumental).

cases.sentence: «Мы с Иваном Петровичем поместились в ___ Алексея», — сказала она, отвечая Степану Аркадьевичу на его вопрос, можно ли курить.
cases.translation: 'Ivan Petrovich and I have settled in Alexei's study,' she said, answering Stepan Arkadyich's question about whether one could smoke.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case here, hence кабинете.

reading.ru: Она встала ему навстречу, не скрывая своей радости увидать его.
reading.question: How did Anna react when Levin arrived?
options: She rose to meet him, not hiding her joy at seeing him
She remained seated and ignored him
She scolded her brother for bringing him
reading.correct: She rose to meet him, not hiding her joy at seeing him
reading.explain: Anna rose to greet Levin, making no secret of her happiness at seeing him.

reading.ru: – Я вас давно знаю и люблю, и по дружбе со Стивой и за вашу жену…  я знала ее очень мало времени, но она оставила во мне впечатление прелестного цветка, именно цветка. И она уж скоро будет матерью!
reading.question: How does Anna describe her impression of Kitty?
options: Like a lovely flower, soon to be a mother
reading.correct: Like a lovely flower, soon to be a mother
reading.explain: Anna says Kitty left her with the impression of a lovely flower, and that she will soon be a mother.

reading.ru: «Не правда ли, необыкновенно хорош», — сказал Степан Аркадьевич, заметив, что Левин взглядывал на портрет.
reading.question: What did Stepan Arkadyich notice Levin doing?
reading.correct: Looking at Anna's portrait
reading.explain: Stepan Arkadyich noticed that Levin kept glancing at the portrait and remarked on how good it was.

reading.ru: Левин покраснел, и чтобы скрыть свое смущение, хотел спросить, давно ли она видела Дарью Александровну.
reading.question: What did Levin want to ask to hide his embarrassment?
options: Whether she had seen Dolly recently
reading.correct: Whether she had seen Dolly recently
reading.explain: To cover his embarrassment, Levin wanted to ask Anna how long ago she had seen Darya Alexandrovna (Dolly).

reading.ru: Она очень рассержена за Гришу на гимназию.
reading.question: Why was Dolly upset, according to Anna?
options: She was angry at the gymnasium because of Grisha
reading.correct: She was angry at the gymnasium because of Grisha
reading.explain: Anna reports that Dolly is very angry at the gymnasium on account of Grisha.

reading.ru: Левин сказал, что французы довели условность в искусстве как никто, и что поэтому они особенную заслугу видят в возвращении к реализму.
reading.question: What point did Levin make about French artists?
options: That they had carried convention in art further than anyone, so they prized a return to realism
That French art was inferior to Russian art
That they had abandoned painting entirely
That they only copied Italian masters
reading.correct: That they had carried convention in art further than anyone, so they prized a return to realism
reading.explain: Levin argued the French had taken artistic convention further than anyone, which is why they saw special merit in returning to realism.

reading.ru: Лицо Анны вдруг все просияло, когда она вдруг оценила эту мысль.
reading.question: How did Anna react to Levin's idea about French art?
options: Her face suddenly lit up as she appreciated the thought
reading.correct: Her face suddenly lit up as she appreciated the thought
reading.explain: Anna's whole face suddenly lit up when she grasped and appreciated Levin's idea.

reading.ru: Прежде столь прекрасное в своем спокойствии ее лицо вдруг выразило странное любопытство, гнев и гордость, но это продолжалось только одну минуту.
reading.question: What sudden change came over Anna's face?
options: It expressed strange curiosity, anger, and pride for a moment
reading.correct: It expressed strange curiosity, anger, and pride for a moment
reading.explain: Anna's face, previously so lovely in its calm, suddenly showed strange curiosity, anger, and pride, though only for a minute.

reading.ru: «Пожалуйста, прикажите подать чай в гостиной».
reading.question: What did Anna ask the English governess to do?
options: Have tea served in the drawing room
reading.correct: Have tea served in the drawing room
reading.explain: Anna asked the English governess to have tea served in the drawing room.

reading.ru: «Прекрасно. Очень способная девочка и милый характер».
reading.question: How did Anna describe the English girl's exam results?
options: Excellent, a very capable girl with a sweet character
reading.correct: Excellent, a very capable girl with a sweet character
reading.explain: Anna said the girl did excellently, calling her very capable with a sweet character.

reading.ru: Граф Алексей Кириллович очень поощрял меня.
reading.question: Who encouraged Anna to take up work at the village school?
reading.correct: Count Alexei Kirillovich (Vronsky)
reading.explain: Anna says that Count Alexei Kirillovich (Vronsky) greatly encouraged her to take up the village school.

reading.ru: Энергия основана на любви, а любовь неоткуда взять, приказать нельзя.
reading.question: What does Anna say about the source of energy for charitable work?
options: It is based on love, and love cannot be commanded or conjured
It can be bought with money
reading.correct: It is based on love, and love cannot be commanded or conjured
reading.explain: Anna says energy is based on love, and love cannot simply be produced or ordered into existence.

reading.ru: У меня не настолько широкое сердце, чтобы полюбить целый приют с гаденькими девочками.
reading.question: What does Anna admit about her capacity for charity work?
options: Her heart isn't broad enough to love a whole orphanage of unappealing girls
She has never tried charity work
She finds all children equally lovable
reading.correct: Her heart isn't broad enough to love a whole orphanage of unappealing girls
reading.explain: Anna confesses that her heart is not broad enough to love a whole orphanage full of unattractive little girls.

reading.ru: «Я знаю про вас, — сказала она Левину, — что вы плохой гражданин, и я вас защищала, как умела.
reading.question: What did Anna tell Levin she had done on his behalf?
options: Defended him against being called a poor citizen
Recommended him for a government post
reading.correct: Defended him against being called a poor citizen
reading.explain: Anna tells Levin she has heard he is a poor citizen and that she defended him as best she could.

reading.ru: «Дайте мне, Анна Аркадьевна», — сказал Варкуев, указывая на книгу.
reading.question: What did Vorkuev ask Anna for?
reading.correct: Her manuscript/book to read
reading.explain: Vorkuev asked Anna to give him the book (her manuscript), pointing at it.

reading.ru: Мое писание — это вроде тех корзиночек из резьбы, которые мне продавала, бывало, Лиза Мерцалова из Острогов.
reading.question: How does Anna compare her own writing?
options: To little carved baskets sold by Liza Mertsalova from the prisons
reading.correct: To little carved baskets sold by Liza Mertsalova from the prisons
reading.explain: Anna modestly compares her writing to the little carved baskets that Liza Mertsalova used to sell her, made in the prisons.

reading.ru: И Левин увидал еще новую черту в этой так необыкновенно понравившейся ему женщине.
reading.question: What new quality did Levin notice in Anna?
options: A new trait, beyond her wit, grace, and beauty
reading.correct: A new trait, beyond her wit, grace, and beauty
reading.explain: Levin noticed yet another new trait, beyond wit, grace, and beauty, in this woman he found so remarkably appealing.

reading.ru: Она от него не хотела скрывать всей тяжести своего положения.
reading.question: What did Anna not want to hide from Levin?
options: The full weight/difficulty of her situation
reading.correct: The full weight/difficulty of her situation
reading.explain: Anna did not want to hide from Levin the full weight of her difficult position.

reading.ru: И прежде так строго осуждавший ее, он теперь по какому-то странному ходу мыслей оправдывал ее.
reading.question: How did Levin's opinion of Anna change during the visit?
options: Having judged her harshly before, he now found himself excusing her
He became even more critical of her
He decided never to see her again
He fell in love with her
reading.correct: Having judged her harshly before, he now found himself excusing her
reading.explain: Levin, who had previously judged Anna so severely, now found himself, through some strange turn of thought, excusing her.

reading.ru: «Я очень рада, что лед сломан».
reading.question: What did Anna say she was glad about as Levin left?
options: That the ice was broken (between them)
That her brother was staying longer
reading.correct: That the ice was broken (between them)
reading.explain: As Levin was leaving, Anna told him she was very glad that the ice had been broken between them.

highlight.question: How well does Anna know Levin's wife?
sentences: – Очень, очень рада, – повторила она, и в устах ее для Левина эти простые слова почему-то получили особенное значение.
– Я вас давно знаю и люблю, и по дружбе со Стивой и за вашу жену…  я знала ее очень мало времени, но она оставила во мне впечатление прелестного цветка, именно цветка.
И она уж скоро будет матерью!
highlight.explain: Sentence 1 mentions that Anna knew Kitty for only a short time but she left a wonderful impression, like a lovely flower.

highlight.question: How does Levin's manner of speaking change when talking with Anna?
sentences: Левин говорил теперь совсем уже не с тем ремесленным отношением к делу, с которым он разговаривал в это утро.
Всякое слово в разговоре с нею получало особенное значение.
И говорить с ней было приятно, еще приятнее было слушать ее.
highlight.explain: Sentences 0 and 1 show that Levin no longer speaks in his usual business-like manner; every word now gains special meaning in conversation with her.

highlight.question: What does Levin's clever thought accomplish?
sentences: Никогда еще ни одна умная вещь, сказанная Левиным, не доставляла ему такого удовольствия, как эта.
Лицо Анны вдруг все просияло, когда она вдруг оценила эту мысль.
Она засмеялась.
highlight.explain: Sentences 1 and 2 show that Anna's face lights up when she appreciates his thought, and she laughs with delight.

highlight.question: What did Anna attempt to do in the countryside according to this passage?
sentences: Граф Алексей Кириллыч очень поощрял меня (произнося слова граф Алексей Кириллыч, она просительно-робко взглянула на Левина, и он невольно отвечал ей почтительным и утвердительным взглядом) – поощрял меня заняться школой в деревне.
Я ходила несколько раз.
Они очень милы, но я не могла привязаться к этому делу.
Вы говорите – энергию.
Энергия основана на любви.
highlight.explain: Sentences 1-3 reveal that she tried to work with a countryside school, visited several times, but could not become attached to the work.

highlight.question: What does Anna say her writing is like?
sentences: – Напрасно сделал.
Мое писанье – это вроде тех корзиночек из резьбы, которые мне продавала, бывало, Лиза Мерцалова из острогов.
Она заведывала острогами в этом обществе, – обратилась она к Левину.
– И эти несчастные делали чудеса терпения.
highlight.explain: Sentences 0 and 1 compare her writing to those carved wooden baskets sold by a woman who managed prisons, made with incredible patience.

highlight.question: What question concerns Levin as Anna speaks with Stepan?
sentences: Она попросила Левина и Воркуева пройти в гостиную, а сама осталась поговорить о чем-то с братом.
«О разводе, о Вронском, о том, что он делает в клубе, обо мне?»
– думал Левин.
И его так волновал вопрос о том, что она говорит со Степаном Аркадьичем, что он почти не слушал того, что рассказывал ему Воркуев о достоинствах написанного Анной Аркадьевной романа для детей.
highlight.explain: Sentences 1 and 2 show Levin wondering what she is telling Stepan, whether about divorce, Vronsky, the club, or himself - so concerned he barely listens to what Vorkuev tells him.
